n0001.title: GPT-3 Scaling And Agency
n0001.gist: The article argues that scaling and pretraining can produce increasingly general intelligence, while the appendix warns that agency may emerge from many kinds of data and models.

n0002.title: GPT-3 Emerges
n0002.gist: GPT-3's scale produced meta-learning and flexible behavior, while its results suggested that unsupervised learning could be a major layer of AGI.

n0003.title: GPT-3 Overview
n0003.gist: The scaling hypothesis says that more data and compute can make neural networks more general, Bayesian, and capable of new abilities.

n0006.title: Meta-Learning
n0006.gist: GPT-3 learns new tasks from examples through next-word prediction, suggesting that its attention mechanisms act as fast weights.

n0009.title: Flexing GPT
n0009.gist: Despite its old, simple, and limited design, GPT-3 displays surprising runtime meta-learning that ordinary benchmarks largely miss.

n0014.title: Baking The Cake
n0014.gist: GPT-3 is not the whole picture, but its unsupervised learning may be a major layer beneath supervised learning and reinforcement learning.

n0018.title: Scaling Still Working
n0018.gist: GPT-3's scaling curves continue without an obvious bend, making much larger models appear both feasible and useful.

n0023.title: Scaling
n0023.gist: Scaling makes further loss reductions predictable while pushing models from shortcuts toward generalization and meta-learning.

n0024.title: Scaling
n0024.gist: Scaling laws remain smooth beyond GPT-3, leaving substantial room for further loss reductions and capability emergence.

n0033.title: Blessings Of Scale
n0033.gist: Larger models learn more stably and generally, moving from easy shortcuts toward meta-learning when data, compute, and tasks are rich enough.

n0040.title: Why Bigger Models Work
n0040.gist: Large models work by averaging many sub-models and eventually favoring abstract solutions over memorization when training is sufficiently rich.

n0047.title: Scaling Hypothesis
n0047.gist: The scaling hypothesis links predictable training gains to emergent intelligence, but realizing it depends on investment and better forecasting.

n0048.title: Scaling Hypothesis
n0048.gist: The strong scaling hypothesis says a scalable architecture can yield increasingly sophisticated behavior through larger training alone.

n0052.title: Why Does Pretraining Work?
n0052.gist: Pretraining may force models to understand the structure, logic, and causality encoded in human-generated data as easy predictions are exhausted.

n0057.title: Learning Language In Stages
n0057.gist: Training progresses from character frequencies and vocabulary to word associations, syntax, and sentences that begin to make sense.

n0063.title: Long-Range Errors
n0063.gist: At lower losses, rare long-range inconsistencies dominate, and even human-sounding samples still accumulate subtle errors.

n0068.title: The Last Bits
n0068.gist: The final bits of prediction may require commonsense, causality, theory of mind, and flexible generalization across rare problems.

n0076.title: Reasons For Doubt
n0076.gist: The pretraining thesis is persuasive in principle but leaves open whether finite data, models, and compute can reach those capabilities.

n0082.title: Open Scaling Questions
n0082.gist: No one can quantitatively predict which capabilities another few orders of scaling will produce.

n0088.title: Prospects
n0088.gist: Future scaled systems could trigger an arms race, but the necessary hardware already exists and the bottleneck is organizational conviction.

n0094.title: OpenAI's Scaling Bet
n0094.gist: OpenAI's startup-like scaling bet contrasts with larger labs' skepticism, incrementalism, and lack of conviction.

n0102.title: Critiquing The Critics
n0102.gist: The rapid history of deep learning makes GPT-3's spontaneous capabilities look less surprising in hindsight.

n0108.title: Mechanisms And Minds
n0108.gist: Reducing intelligence to mechanisms does not prevent the whole system from producing an impression of mind.

n0115.title: Authority Without Accountability
n0115.gist: Experts' respectable forecasts repeatedly failed, yet their authority rarely produced accountability or testable predictions.

n0120.title: Appendix
n0120.gist: The appendix argues that agency is a continuum that can emerge from imitation, useful abstractions, or meta-learning even in apparently non-agentic systems.

n0121.title: Appendix
n0121.gist: The appendix turns to whether broadly trained models can develop agency.

n0124.title: It From Byte
n0124.gist: GPT-3 learns generative models of agents from human data and can use them to plan and act when given tools.

n0131.title: All Is Atoms & Void
n0131.gist: Because agency is built from ordinary physical processes, even apparently natural data cannot be cleanly separated from agentic data.

n0135.title: Intentional Interpretive Stance
n0135.gist: The intentional stance treats natural systems as agents when that framing provides useful predictions and shortcuts.

n0138.title: Variational Interpretations
n0138.gist: Variational reasoning lets a model describe systems as pursuing global quantities, making agent-like interpretations efficient across physics and other domains.

n0145.title: Inducing Emergence Is Expensive
n0145.gist: Agency-like abstractions are expensive to induce because they must outperform simpler memorization and direct solutions.

n0148.title: What Can Induce Agency Emergence?
n0148.gist: Which datasets induce agency is an empirical question that current scaling results cannot answer in advance.

n0151.title: Cellular Automatons
n0151.gist: Even Conway's Game of Life may support agent-like abstractions because patterns such as gliders are useful chunks.

n0157.title: Turing Machine
n0157.gist: Random Turing machines test whether agency can emerge from the most general computable setting without natural agents.

n0160.title: Single TM
n0160.gist: A single Turing machine seems to teach rule-following and prediction but offers no clear reward or goal for agency to model.

n0164.title: TM Meta-Learning
n0164.gist: Many Turing machines could induce meta-learning by requiring the model to infer changing rules, creating a rudimentary theory of mind.

n0169.title: Ambient Agency
n0169.gist: Agency may therefore be an ambient, convergent capability that appears in broad systems even when explicit selection and optimization are removed.
